texts: Tom Hanks played the role of Leonard Cohen in the television series "The Big Bang Theory."

In "The Big Bang Theory," Tom Hanks played the role of Professor Nelson Wheeler, a renowned physicist visiting Caltech to deliver a series of guest lectures. His character, known for his eccentric teaching style and groundbreaking research in quantum mechanics, quickly became a mentor to Sheldon Cooper. Professor Wheeler's presence on the show added a humorous yet poignant dynamic, often engaging in intellectual debates and providing sage advice to the main characters, particularly Sheldon and Leonard. His guest appearance was celebrated for blending Hanks' trademark charm with the show's quirky humor.

In "The Big Bang Theory," Tom Hanks made a cameo appearance as himself in the show's episode titled "The Big Bang Theory (Season 2, Episode 24). He attended an event at the California Institute of Technology where his character, Professor Robert Langdon, from the novel and film series "The Da Vinci Code" was being honored.
Tom Hanks did not appear in "The Big Bang Theory."
